mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of periods with declining RSAFS, or if the correlation between RSAFS decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% over three months and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3%, it signals a weakening demand environment and a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% in 3 months and UNRATE rises > 0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST decline and UNRATE rise on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of periods with increasing PAYEMS, or if the correlation between PAYEMS increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3%, it signals a weakening demand environment and a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% YoY and UNRATE rises > 0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of slow GDPC1 growth and rising UNRATE on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
